stem: Which is the CORRECT order of volatility, from MOST volatile to LEAST volatile?
choices: Disk → Memory → CPU registers/cache → Backup tapes
CPU registers/cache → System memory (RAM) → Network state → Disk → Backup tapes
explanation: RFC 3227 order of volatility: registers/cache → memory → network state/processes → disk → remote logs → backup tapes. Capture in this order to preserve the most volatile evidence first. The other choices reverse or scramble the sequence.

web_sources.title: FlashGenius: IR for CISSP 2026 — NIST 800-61 + chain of custody

stem: Which is the BEST practice for maintaining chain of custody?
choices: Pass evidence informally between team members
Document every transfer, location, and access — preserving an unbroken record from collection through court
Store evidence on a shared drive any team member can access
Skip documentation if pressed for time
explanation: Chain of custody is a documented record proving evidence integrity from seizure to court. Unbroken chain is essential for admissibility. Informal passes, shared access, and skipped documentation all break it.

web_sources.title: FlashGenius: IR for CISSP 2026 — NIST 800-61 + chain of custody

stem: Which technique BEST verifies that a forensic image is byte-for-byte identical to the original media?
choices: Cryptographic hashing (e.g., SHA-256) of source and image; the digests must match
Boot the image and check the user interface
explanation: Hash comparison (commonly SHA-256; MD5 is acceptable for forensic verification despite being broken cryptographically because the use case is integrity, not adversarial collision resistance) provides cryptographic proof. Visual checks and boot tests miss subtle changes.

web_sources.title: FlashGenius: IR for CISSP 2026 — NIST 800-61 + chain of custody

stem: Which type of evidence is MOST authoritative in legal proceedings?
explanation: Best evidence (the original document or media, or its forensic image) is preferred. Secondary evidence (copies) is less weighty. Hearsay is generally inadmissible without exception. Demonstrative evidence (charts, models) supports but does not replace original evidence.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which RAID level provides REDUNDANCY without the write penalty of parity calculation by writing to two disks simultaneously?
explanation: RAID 1 mirrors data across two disks — no parity, full redundancy at 50% storage efficiency. RAID 0 stripes for performance with no redundancy. RAID 5 distributes parity (write penalty). RAID 6 has dual parity (more write penalty, more fault tolerance).

web_sources.title: CISSPrep: Data Backup

stem: Which RAID level can survive the loss of TWO drives simultaneously?
explanation: RAID 6 uses dual parity — surviving any two-drive failure. RAID 5 survives one. RAID 1 survives one (the mirror copy). RAID 10 (1+0) survives the loss of multiple drives but only if they aren't both members of the same mirror pair.

web_sources.title: CISSPrep: Data Backup

stem: Which alternate processing site type contains hardware ready to use, with current data restored, and is the FASTEST to bring online?
explanation: Hot sites are continually maintained, fully equipped, and often have near-real-time data — ready in minutes/hours. Warm sites have hardware but stale data (12+ hours). Cold sites have only space and utilities. Mobile sites are trailers brought to a location.

web_sources.title: Cybrary: CISSP — Hot, Cold, and Warm Sites

stem: An organisation does a full backup Sunday and DIFFERENTIAL backups Monday-Saturday. What is needed to restore Friday's data?
choices: Sunday full + Thursday's differential + Friday's incremental
explanation: Differential backups capture changes since the last FULL — only the most recent differential is needed. Incremental backups would require all increments. Differentials grow over the week (slower backups, faster restores).

web_sources.title: CISSPrep: Data Backup

stem: Which backup type captures only data changed SINCE THE LAST INCREMENTAL OR FULL BACKUP?
explanation: Incrementals capture changes since the previous backup of any type — fast to back up, slow to restore (need full + every incremental in chain). Differentials capture since the last full — slower to back up, faster to restore.

web_sources.title: CISSPrep: Data Backup

stem: Which backup strategy is recommended by CISA / industry as the '3-2-1 rule'?
choices: 3 backups per day, 2 hours retention, 1 admin
explanation: 3-2-1 = three copies of data, on two different media types, with one copy offsite. Modern variants (3-2-1-1-0) add an immutable copy and zero errors after verification. The other choices misinterpret the term.

web_sources.title: CISSPrep: Data Backup

stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a maintenance window?
choices: Provide an authorised, communicated period for changes that may impact availability or service
explanation: Maintenance windows aggregate authorised disruption, with stakeholder notification, rollback plans, and controlled risk. The other choices are unrelated to the security/availability rationale.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the PRIMARY purpose of a Change Advisory Board (CAB)?
choices: Evaluate proposed changes for risk, business impact, and authorisation prior to implementation
explanation: CAB authorises changes balancing operational, security, and business risk. Code-commit review is dev-team scope. Hiring and finance are unrelated. Emergency Change Advisory Boards (eCAB) handle urgent changes with abbreviated process.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a baseline configuration?
choices: Define an approved, secure starting state for systems and detect drift over time
explanation: Baselines define the approved state; configuration management tools (Ansible, Puppet, Chef, GPO) detect and remediate drift. They complement patch management. Licence compliance is an inventory function.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which capability does SOAR ADD over SIEM?
choices: Orchestration and automated response playbooks across security tools
explanation: SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, Response) ties tools together with playbooks (containment, enrichment, ticket creation) — extending SIEM's correlation. Logging and other choices are SIEM or other tools' jobs.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which technology BUILDS BASELINES of user/entity behaviour and alerts on deviations?
explanation: UEBA (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) profiles normal behaviour and surfaces anomalies (impossible-travel logins, unusual data access). WAF protects HTTP, DLP prevents data leakage, NAC controls access. UEBA is increasingly bundled into SIEM/XDR.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which BCP plan focuses specifically on the technology recovery aspects?
explanation: DRP (Disaster Recovery Plan) is the technology-recovery subset of the broader BCP. Crisis communications addresses messaging. COOP (Continuity of Operations Plan) is the federal-government continuity term. BCP is the overarching plan.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which BCP test type is MOST disruptive but provides the HIGHEST ASSURANCE of recovery capability?
explanation: Full-interruption tests shift production to the DR site, demonstrating real recovery — disruptive and risky if it fails, but the highest-assurance test. Tabletop/walkthrough/simulation are progressively more involved but stop short of cutover.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Recovery Strategies Mindmap — Domain 7

stem: Which control is MOST EFFECTIVE for detecting data exfiltration to attacker-controlled cloud storage?
choices: Allow all outbound traffic and trust users
DLP egress inspection plus outbound proxy with TLS interception (where policy allows) or destination categorisation
explanation: Outbound proxies with destination categorisation/blocking (and DLP content inspection where TLS is broken with policy) detect/block exfiltration. Trusting all egress and disabling internet are extremes. Opening all ports defeats the firewall.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which factor MOST influences whether to choose a hot, warm, or cold site?
explanation: Lower RTO requires more pre-positioned infrastructure (hot site = lowest RTO, highest cost). Cold site is cheap but has long RTO. The exam expects RTO/cost trade-off as the driver.

web_sources.title: Cybrary: CISSP — Hot, Cold, and Warm Sites

stem: Which is the BEST cadence for routine vulnerability scanning of internet-facing assets?
choices: At least monthly, with continuous scanning preferred where feasible
explanation: Internet-facing surfaces change rapidly; monthly is the modern minimum, with continuous scanning increasingly common (PCI-DSS requires quarterly external + scans after change). Annual is too infrequent.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: An emergency change is needed to mitigate active exploitation. What is the BEST process?
choices: Use the emergency change process (eCAB approval, retroactive documentation, rollback plan)
Wait for the next scheduled CAB
explanation: Emergency change processes balance speed with accountability — eCAB approval, simplified documentation, retroactive review. Bypassing entirely or implementing silently fails audit. Waiting prolongs exposure.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST policy for protecting log integrity from a privileged user on the source system?
choices: Privileged users administer the log destination too
Forward logs to a system the privileged user CANNOT administer (separation of duties)
explanation: SoD between source and log destination prevents tampering. Encrypting locally is bypassable by the admin. Skipping privileged-action logging is a serious gap. Choice A explicitly defeats SoD.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for shoulder-surfing in open-plan offices?
choices: Privacy filters on screens, screen-lock policies, and physical workspace orientation
explanation: Physical/visual privacy controls reduce shoulder-surfing exposure. Trust alone is insufficient. Disabling login is impractical. Headphones are unrelated.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Who has the AUTHORITY to declare a disaster and trigger the DR plan?
choices: The first responder on the scene
An executive or designated incident commander, per the documented BCP
explanation: Disaster declaration follows a defined chain of authority documented in the BCP — typically an executive or BC manager. Ad-hoc declaration creates chaos. The exam consistently picks the documented authority.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST description of clipping levels in monitoring?
choices: A maximum login retry threshold below which actions are tolerated
A way to trim long log files
explanation: Clipping levels suppress alert noise — e.g., ignore single failed logins but alert at 5+. They balance noise vs. signal. The other choices are unrelated. Modern UEBA replaces simple thresholds with adaptive baselines.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST description of an administrative investigation?
choices: Internal investigation of policy violations or misconduct, governed by HR and legal
explanation: Administrative investigations look at internal policy violations (acceptable use, harassment) — typically led by HR/legal/internal investigators. Civil and criminal investigations have different standards. Vendor audits are separate.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which evidence standard typically applies to CIVIL litigation?
explanation: Civil cases use preponderance ('more likely than not', >50%). Criminal cases use beyond-reasonable-doubt. Some administrative cases use clear-and-convincing. Probable cause is for warrants/arrests.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: What is the PRIMARY risk of installing patches in production WITHOUT testing?
choices: Patches may break functionality or introduce regressions, causing outages
explanation: Patches occasionally break things — testing in lower environments and staged rollouts mitigate that. Manager-mindset: balance patch speed (security) against testing rigor (stability) per risk.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST policy for handling removable media in high-security environments?
choices: Allow all USB devices for convenience
Block by default; allow specific approved devices via device control with encryption and DLP
Disable USB ports physically only on legacy systems
Trust users to use only personal devices
explanation: Default-deny + device control + encryption + DLP defends against the BadUSB / wholesale exfil pattern. Allowing all USB or trusting users defeats security. Physical-port disabling alone is incomplete.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST way to validate a backup is RESTORABLE?
choices: Trust the backup software's success message
Periodically perform a full restore in a test environment and verify integrity
Look at the backup completion log only
explanation: Restoration tests are the only true validation. Many organisations have discovered backups were unrestorable AT the moment they needed them. Vendor success messages and completion logs are inputs but not proof.

web_sources.title: CISSPrep: Data Backup

stem: Which is the BEST control for privileged session management?
choices: Brokered sessions via a PAM gateway with recording, MFA, and time bounds
Local admin accounts on every system
explanation: PAM session brokering provides recording, MFA enforcement, and time bounds — a major detective + preventive control. The other choices represent classic anti-patterns.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Who is ULTIMATELY accountable for the BCP program in an organisation?
explanation: Like other governance functions, BCP accountability rests with senior leadership. The BCP coordinator is responsible for execution. IT and vendors are participants. Manager-mindset: accountability rests with the highest authority.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST way to ensure detections remain effective as the threat landscape evolves?
choices: Set them up once and forget
Continuously tune detections based on threat intel, false-positive feedback, and ATT&CK coverage gaps
explanation: Detections rot — environment changes, attacker tradecraft evolves. Continuous tuning + ATT&CK coverage analysis keeps them effective. Disabling noisy detections rather than tuning is dangerous.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST control for protecting data in transit BETWEEN data centers across a public internet path?
choices: IPsec site-to-site VPN with strong AEAD ciphers
explanation: Site-to-site IPsec with AEAD (e.g., AES-GCM) provides confidentiality, integrity, and authentication. MD5 + TCP, FTP, and Telnet are insecure. Modern alternatives include WireGuard and TLS-based mesh tunnels.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST single source of the most-recent attacker tradecraft?
choices: Threat intelligence feeds curated for the organisation's sector and ATT&CK mapping
explanation: Tailored threat intel + ATT&CK keeps detections current. Old whitepapers and general media lag attacker innovation. The exam favors current, sector-specific intelligence.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST description of a 'cloud DR' strategy?
choices: Storing backups on a personal cloud account
Provisioning DR capacity in a cloud provider with automated failover and data replication
explanation: Cloud DR uses elastic provider capacity (warm or cold replica) with replication, automated failover, and pay-as-you-go economics. The other choices are not strategies. Multi-region cloud architectures are a modern cloud-DR pattern.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Recovery Strategies Mindmap — Domain 7

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for a zero-day vulnerability with no available patch?
choices: Apply compensating controls (network segmentation, WAF rules, IPS signatures, virtual patching) until vendor patch is available
explanation: Compensating controls limit exposure while waiting for patches. Manager-mindset: defense in depth means you can buy time. Disabling monitoring or premature disclosure are anti-patterns.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST first step when a SIEM rule generates excessive false positives?
choices: Investigate the trigger context, narrow the rule to specific patterns, and tune thresholds
Ignore all alerts from the rule
explanation: Tuning preserves the detection while reducing noise. Disabling silently leaves a gap. Ignoring alerts is dangerous. The exam favors investigate-and-tune over disable.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for the risk of assets being decommissioned WITHOUT proper sanitisation?
choices: Tracked decommissioning workflow with sanitisation per NIST 800-88, certificate of destruction, and sign-off
Use a single shared decommissioning bin
explanation: Documented workflow with sanitisation, certificate of destruction, and sign-off is the audit-ready answer. The other choices are anti-patterns leading to data leakage.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which BCP plan element addresses keeping personnel safe and accounted for during a disaster?
explanation: Crisis management/occupant emergency plans cover life safety — evacuation, headcount, sheltering. IT recovery is separate. Life safety always comes BEFORE technology recovery (a recurring exam theme).

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST principle for protecting against the insider-threat scenario of a single admin shutting down logging then exfiltrating data?
choices: Separation of duties and dual-control for sensitive operations (e.g., log management requires two distinct approvals)
explanation: Dual-control / SoD prevents single-point compromise. The other choices either explicitly enable or normalise the risk. Manager-mindset: design controls so single rogue actors cannot complete the kill chain alone.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the PRIMARY purpose of a honeypot in security operations?
choices: A decoy system to attract, detect, and study attackers without exposing real assets
explanation: Honeypots are decoys with no legitimate users — any interaction is suspicious by definition. They provide high-quality, low-noise detection. Honeynets extend the concept to whole network segments. Legal considerations (entrapment) usually do not apply because attackers must initiate.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST way to enforce the principle of least privilege for system administrators?
choices: Standard accounts for daily work + named admin accounts for specific tasks + JIT elevation for privileged actions
explanation: Separating daily work from privileged work, then JIT-elevating only when needed, minimises standing privilege. Shared roots and always-root configurations are anti-patterns.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which document should establish RTO and RPO for each business process?
explanation: BIA enumerates critical processes and assigns RTO/RPO/MTD/WRT. The other documents serve different purposes. The exam consistently associates BIA with these time metrics.

stem: Which capability does EDR provide beyond traditional antivirus?
choices: Continuous endpoint telemetry, behavioural detection, response actions (isolate, kill, retrieve files), and forensic data
explanation: EDR provides telemetry + detection + response + forensic capabilities — far beyond signature AV. Many EDR products also support threat hunting via stored telemetry. Choices A, C, D describe other tool categories.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST control for protecting cryptographic keys at runtime?
choices: Use a hardware security module (HSM) or platform key vault with strict access policy
explanation: HSMs/platform key vaults (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) protect keys with hardware-rooted security and policy controls. The other choices are catastrophic anti-patterns.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST first source for understanding the criticality of a newly disclosed vulnerability?
choices: Vendor advisory + CVE entry + CVSS scoring + KEV (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities) status
explanation: Authoritative sources (vendor + CVE + CVSS + CISA KEV) provide signal needed to prioritise. Twitter is noisy/early-stage; helpdesk tickets and marketing don't reflect technical risk.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which is the BEST description of 'need to know' in operational security?
choices: Anyone who asks should be told
Access to information should be limited to those whose duties require it, even when general clearance allows broader access
Need to know is a synonym for least privilege
Need to know applies only to government
explanation: Need-to-know restricts access by job-required justification — narrower than clearance/role. Least privilege is related but broader (covering rights, not just information access). Need-to-know is widely applied in commercial contexts (M&A, HR, legal).

web_sources.title: DestCert: Insights into CISSP Domain 7 — Security Operations

stem: Which SDLC model proceeds linearly through phases (requirements → design → implementation → testing → deployment) without revisiting earlier phases?
explanation: Waterfall is sequential — each phase completes before the next begins. Agile is iterative. Spiral is risk-driven and iterative. DevSecOps is continuous. Waterfall remains common in safety-critical/regulated domains where rigor is required.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which SDLC approach delivers working software in short iterative cycles with continuous customer feedback?
explanation: Agile (Scrum, Kanban, XP) emphasises iteration, customer feedback, and incremental delivery. The Agile Manifesto (2001) frames the value system. The other choices describe sequential or rigid approaches.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which approach INTEGRATES security throughout the development pipeline (planning, coding, building, testing, deployment, monitoring)?
choices: DevSecOps with shift-left and continuous security testing
Outsourcing all security to external auditors
explanation: DevSecOps embeds security into CI/CD with automation (SAST, DAST, SCA, IaC scanning, secrets detection) — shifting left into design/code rather than waiting for release. The other choices reflect anti-patterns or partial solutions.

web_sources.title: Aikido: NIST SSDF (SP 800-218) Secure Software Development Explained
GitHub: OWASP DevSecOps Guideline

stem: Which is the BEST description of OWASP SAMM?
choices: A prescriptive software-security maturity framework with five business functions and four maturity levels
explanation: OWASP SAMM (Software Assurance Maturity Model) helps organisations measure and improve software security posture across Governance, Design, Implementation, Verification, and Operations. The other choices describe different artefacts entirely.

web_sources.title: OWASP: Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM)
Info-Savvy: CISSP Maturity Models

stem: Which maturity model is descriptive — based on observed practices in real software security programs at participating organisations?
explanation: BSIMM (Building Security In Maturity Model) is descriptive — observed activities at member firms. SAMM is prescriptive (recommendations). CMMI is process maturity (general). ITIL is service management. The exam differentiates BSIMM vs SAMM.

web_sources.title: Info-Savvy: CISSP Maturity Models
Infosec Institute: Software maturity models for AppSec

stem: Which model assesses PROCESS maturity from Initial (1) through Optimising (5)?
explanation: CMMI uses five maturity levels: Initial, Managed, Defined, Quantitatively Managed, Optimising. SAMM uses four levels per practice. BSIMM is descriptive. ISO 27034 is software security guidance.

web_sources.title: Info-Savvy: CISSP Maturity Models

stem: Which OWASP Top 10:2021 category covers the FAILURE to enforce restrictions on what authenticated users can do (e.g., URL tampering to access another user's data)?
explanation: A01 Broken Access Control became #1 in 2021. Examples: forced browsing to admin URLs, IDOR (insecure direct object reference), missing function-level checks. Cryptographic failures = data-protection issues. Injection = SQL, command. Insecure design is broader.

web_sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2021 — Next Steps

stem: Which OWASP Top 10:2021 category specifically covers vulnerable third-party libraries used in applications?
choices: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
explanation: A06 specifically addresses libraries with known vulnerabilities (e.g., Log4Shell). SCA (Software Composition Analysis) and dependency hygiene mitigate it. A05 is misconfiguration; A07 is authn; A08 is supply-chain integrity (CI/CD compromise, signed artefacts).

web_sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2021 — Next Steps

stem: What is a TOCTOU (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) vulnerability?
choices: A race condition where a resource is checked then used, but its state can change between check and use
explanation: TOCTOU exploits a window between an authorisation/state check and the operation. Example: check file ownership, then open file — attacker swaps the path with a symlink in between. Mitigation: atomic operations, file descriptors instead of paths. CWE-367 captures this.

web_sources.title: CQR: TOCTTOU Race Conditions
CWE-367: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU)

stem: Which is the MOST EFFECTIVE primary defence against buffer overflows in modern code?
choices: Use memory-safe languages (Rust, Go, managed languages); for C/C++ use safe APIs, bounds checking, and OS mitigations (ASLR, DEP, stack canaries)
explanation: Memory-safe languages eliminate whole classes of overflow. For unavoidable C/C++, defensive APIs (snprintf instead of strcpy), bounds checks, and OS mitigations layer defenses. Hoping is not a control. Disabling error messages hides issues. Larger stacks don't fix overflows.

web_sources.title: OWASP: Buffer Overflow

stem: Which is the BEST defence against XSS (cross-site scripting)?
choices: Output encoding contextual to the destination (HTML, JS, URL, CSS) plus a strict Content Security Policy
Hope users never see the input
explanation: Context-aware output encoding (HTML body vs attribute vs JS context) is the canonical fix. CSP provides defense in depth. Substring stripping is bypassable. Disabling JS breaks apps. Manager-mindset: prevent at output, not just at input.

web_sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2021 — Next Steps

stem: Which is the BEST defence against CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery)?
choices: Anti-CSRF tokens (synchroniser pattern) plus SameSite cookies
Use only HTTPS without other controls
explanation: CSRF tokens that the attacker cannot read combined with SameSite=Lax/Strict cookies block the canonical attack. Referer is unreliable. User-agent can be spoofed. HTTPS alone does not defend against CSRF.

web_sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2021 — Next Steps

stem: Which is the BEST first step toward integrating security into a CI/CD pipeline?
choices: Add a manual security review at the very end
Embed automated SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, and IaC checks as gates earlier in the pipeline
Disable failing tests to keep the pipeline green
explanation: Shift-left automation in CI/CD catches issues at low cost; gating prevents merging known issues. The other choices either delay security or weaken it.

web_sources.title: Practical DevSecOps: Integrating Security into CI/CD Pipelines
GitHub: OWASP DevSecOps Guideline

stem: Which is the PRIMARY security benefit of Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC)?
choices: Repeatable, reviewable, scannable definitions of infrastructure that enable policy-as-code and drift detection
explanation: IaC (Terraform, CloudFormation, ARM, Bicep, Pulumi) makes infrastructure auditable, reviewable, and scannable (Checkov, tfsec, KICS). Choices C, D are wrong. Drift detection is a major operational benefit.

web_sources.title: Aikido: NIST SSDF (SP 800-218) Secure Software Development Explained

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for software supply-chain attacks (e.g., compromised dependency packages)?
choices: Trust all packages from public registries
SCA, SBOM, provenance verification (SLSA framework), pinning to known-good versions, and private registry mirrors
explanation: SCA + SBOM + provenance + pinning + mirroring layers defenses. The SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) framework formalises supply-chain integrity. Choices A, C, D are extremes that don't work.

web_sources.title: Aikido: NIST SSDF (SP 800-218) Secure Software Development Explained

stem: Which OWASP project provides verifiable security requirements for web applications?
explanation: OWASP ASVS provides three verification levels (1-3) of security requirements for web apps. Top 10 is awareness. ZAP is a DAST tool. Cheat sheets are reference docs. ASVS is the standard for assurance-driven secure development.

web_sources.title: OWASP: Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS)

stem: Which is the BEST description of an INFERENCE attack on a database?
choices: Combining individually authorised queries to deduce information that the user is not authorised to see directly
explanation: Inference attacks exploit aggregation/correlation across legitimate queries. Mitigations: limit query patterns, polyinstantiation, differential privacy, statistical noise. Choices A, C, D describe other attacks.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which database technique stores DIFFERENT VALUES under the SAME primary key for different security levels?
explanation: Polyinstantiation stores multiple instances of the same logical record at different classification levels — preventing covert channels via existence inference. Inference is the attack; aggregation combines authorized data; normalization is a relational design technique.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which database property ensures that transactions are 'all or nothing' (a partially completed transaction is rolled back)?
explanation: ACID's Atomicity ensures transactions complete fully or not at all. Consistency: transitions valid states only. Isolation: concurrent transactions don't interfere. Durability: committed data survives failures. ACID is fundamental to relational databases.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which is the BEST description of API rate limiting?
choices: Restricting the number of requests per identity/source per time window to defend against abuse and DoS
explanation: Rate limiting per identity/IP/key bounds abuse, brute force, and accidental misuse. Implemented in API gateways or app middleware. Choices A, C, D are unrelated.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which is the BEST authentication mechanism for service-to-service API calls in modern architectures?
choices: OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant with short-lived tokens (or mTLS)
explanation: OAuth 2.0 client_credentials with short-lived tokens (or mTLS for workload identity) is the modern standard. API keys in URLs leak in logs. Basic auth without TLS exposes credentials. Hardcoded creds are catastrophic.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which artifact LISTS the components and dependencies in a software product?
explanation: SBOM (SPDX or CycloneDX format) lists components, versions, licences, and supply-chain provenance — required by US Executive Order 14028. Choices A, C, D do not provide structured component lists.

web_sources.title: Aikido: NIST SSDF (SP 800-218) Secure Software Development Explained

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for OS command injection in code that builds shell commands from user input?
choices: Avoid shells entirely; use parameterised APIs (e.g., subprocess with argv list, not shell=True) and strict allow-lists for any required pass-through
Trust user input from authenticated sessions
explanation: Avoid shells; parameterise the call. If shell is unavoidable, use strict allow-lists. String concatenation is the bug. Trusting authenticated input ignores authorisation. Hashing destroys legitimate input.

web_sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2021 — Next Steps

stem: Which is the BEST defence against insecure deserialization (CWE-502)?
choices: Use plain pickle / Java native serialization
Avoid native serialization for untrusted data; prefer simple data formats (JSON), strict schemas, and integrity checks
explanation: Native serialization (pickle, Java ObjectInputStream, .NET BinaryFormatter) on untrusted input enables RCE. JSON with strict schema validation is safer. Choices A, C are anti-patterns.

web_sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2021 — Next Steps

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for accidental commit of secrets to source repositories?
choices: Pre-commit hooks + CI secret scanning + a secrets manager + git history rewrite/rotation if leaks occur
Use a single password file in the root
explanation: Multilayer defenses (hooks, CI scanning, vault) plus rotation when leaks occur. Trust alone fails; password files and email are catastrophic.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for malicious or accidental commits to protected branches?
choices: Require signed commits, branch protection rules, code review, and CODEOWNERS approval
explanation: Defence in depth: signed commits + branch protection + review + CODEOWNERS = comprehensive. Direct pushes and trust without review violate SoD. The exam favours separation, not trust.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which threat-modeling step BEST aligns with 'identifying entry points and trust boundaries'?
choices: Decomposing the application and drawing data-flow diagrams (DFDs) with trust boundaries
explanation: DFDs with trust boundaries are the canonical artefact in STRIDE-style threat modeling — entry points, assets, trust transitions become visible. Choices A, C, D are unrelated to threat modeling.

web_sources.title: DestCert: Threat Modeling Methodologies — STRIDE, PASTA, DREAD

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for vulnerable container images?
choices: Scan images at build, sign images, use minimal base images, run as non-root, and apply runtime image policies
explanation: Build-time scanning + minimal base + non-root + runtime policy = layered defense. Trust without verification is the typical anti-pattern. Root containers expand blast radius.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery, OWASP A10:2021)?
choices: Use allow-lists of permitted destinations, deny RFC 1918/private/metadata endpoints, and use a dedicated egress proxy
explanation: SSRF is mitigated by explicit destination allow-listing, blocking metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254 in cloud), and routing egress through a controlled proxy. Choices A, C, D are anti-patterns.

web_sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2021 — Next Steps

stem: Which is the BEST policy for handling a critical CVE in a third-party library used across many services?
choices: Wait until the next quarterly upgrade window
Inventory affected services via SBOM, prioritise by exposure, patch through accelerated change management, and verify
Replace the library with an in-house version overnight
explanation: SBOM-driven inventory + risk-based prioritisation + accelerated change management + verification is the manager-mindset answer. Quarterly waits accumulate risk; in-house overnight rewrites introduce new risks.

web_sources.title: Aikido: NIST SSDF (SP 800-218) Secure Software Development Explained

stem: Which is the BEST description of a 'security gate' in the SDLC?
choices: A defined checkpoint where security criteria must be met before progressing to the next phase
explanation: Security gates (e.g., 'no critical SAST findings before merge', 'no high CVEs before deploy') enforce security criteria at phase transitions. Choices A, C, D are unrelated or partial.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for the risk of overly permissive cloud IAM policies?
choices: Apply least privilege, use scoped roles, automated drift detection (e.g., IAM Access Analyzer), and JIT elevation
explanation: Least privilege + scoped roles + drift detection + JIT is the manager-mindset answer. The other choices are catastrophic anti-patterns. Cloud IAM misconfiguration is one of the top cloud risks per CSA.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation when integrating a third-party SaaS that processes customer data?
choices: Vendor risk assessment, DPA (Data Processing Agreement), evidence of SOC 2 Type II, scoped permissions, and offboarding plan
explanation: Risk-based assessment + DPA + audit evidence + scoped access + offboarding plan is the standard manager-mindset answer. Other choices skip duty.

web_sources.title: DestCert: CISSP Domain 8 — Software Development Security Guide 2025

stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of input validation as a defensive coding practice?
choices: Reject inputs that violate expected format, length, type, and range — reducing attack surface
explanation: Input validation enforces format/length/type/range; combine with output encoding contextually for full defence in depth. Choices A, C, D are wrong. 'Validate input, encode output' is the canonical pairing.

web_sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2021 — Next Steps

stem: Which is the BEST description of 'fail securely' as a secure-design principle?
choices: Crash the system on any error
When errors occur, default to a secure state (deny access, do not expose stack traces, do not leak data)
explanation: Fail-securely means errors don't leave the system in an insecure state — deny by default, suppress sensitive error info to clients, log securely. Crashing or continuing blindly are anti-patterns.

stem: Which is the BEST control for protecting CI/CD pipeline secrets and tokens?
choices: Use a secrets manager / OIDC federation with short-lived tokens; restrict repo permissions and audit usage
explanation: Modern CI/CD uses OIDC federation (GitHub Actions to AWS/GCP/Azure) for short-lived tokens, and secrets managers for credentials. Hardcoding and printing leak secrets. The exam favours short-lived, vaulted credentials.

stem: Which is a UNIQUE security concern with GraphQL APIs that REST APIs DON'T typically face directly?
choices: Query complexity / depth attacks where attackers can craft expensive queries
explanation: GraphQL's flexibility lets clients request deeply nested or expensive queries (denial of service via complexity). Mitigations: query depth limits, complexity scoring, persisted queries. REST exposes fixed endpoints with bounded shapes.

stem: Which is the BEST description of 'privacy by design'?
choices: Adding a privacy notice at the end
Embedding privacy considerations (data minimisation, purpose limitation, consent) into the system from the design phase
explanation: Privacy-by-design (Ann Cavoukian, GDPR Article 25) bakes privacy in from inception — data minimisation, default settings favour privacy, transparency. Choices A, C, D are afterthoughts.

stem: Which is the BEST mitigation for hardcoded credentials in source code?
choices: Remove from code, rotate the credential, store in a secrets manager, scan repos for further leaks, and add pre-commit/CI scanning
explanation: Removing alone is insufficient because git history retains the secret — rotate, scan history, prevent recurrence. Choices A, C, D fall short.

stem: Which NIST publication codifies a Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) of practices?
explanation: NIST SP 800-218 (SSDF) defines four practice groups (Prepare the Org, Protect the Software, Produce Well-Secured Software, Respond to Vulnerabilities). 800-115 is testing; 800-37 is RMF; 800-53 is controls catalog.
